core_direction: Use specialist agents for research, design, build, review, and trend analysis
Treat authn, authz, approval, policy, and audit as first-class concerns
Favor small safe increments over broad speculative refactors

phase_7_policy_hardening_scope.intent: Harden live-run policy operations after phase_6 by enforcing explicit auth boundaries and routing controls without relaxing strict completion policy.
must_enforce: Keep strict gate completed-only semantics
Do not treat revision_requested as strict success
Use explicit allowlist checks for effective agent/provider/model in strict runs
Keep operator vs approver authority boundaries auditable
Record deny reasons and override usage in audit/manifest evidence

operation_modes.normal: Day-to-day mode with operational flexibility and full evidence capture.
operation_modes.strict: Completed-only verification mode with explicit policy checks and fallback budgets.
operation_modes.breakglass: Exception path requiring explicit reason, actor traceability, and policy evidence markers.

non_goals: No new provider onboarding as part of policy hardening
No architecture rewrite to implement phase_7 controls

phase_8_product_hardening_scope.intent: Harden the local operational package for commercial pilot onboarding without weakening established auth/policy gates.
must_enforce: Preserve strict completed-only semantics and phase_7 policy invariants
Treat sqlite as the default local operational backend with explicit recovery guidance
Keep OpenClaw integration evidence and diagnostics first-class in runbooks and manifests
Improve operator-facing startup/readiness/support workflows without broad architecture changes

focus_areas.operational_baseline: Default to repeatable sqlite-backed startup and readiness execution profiles.
focus_areas.onboarding_packaging: Unify quick-start, startup, readiness, and operator docs for pilot handoff.
focus_areas.supportability: Strengthen failure triage and evidence-capture paths for faster incident isolation.

non_goals: No auth or policy gate relaxation introduced in phase_7
No orchestrator architecture rewrite for commercial packaging

must_preserve: Authenticated actor resolution on protected approval endpoints
Server-side actor authority over client-provided actor fields
Audit visibility for authentication, authorization, override, and approval decisions
Backward-compatible behavior unless a deprecation is explicitly documented
do_not_do: Do not merge Intake and Orchestrator responsibilities
Do not let provider-specific logic leak into core orchestration
Do not weaken strict_mode or policy enforcement silently
Do not add new infrastructure or dependencies without justification
Do not change schema or migration behavior without review
Do not replace tested behavior with speculative redesign
continue_if: Tests for the touched area pass
The change fits the current roadmap phase
No auth/policy/security boundary changes are required
pause_if: Verification fails and root cause is not yet isolated
The next step is unclear from roadmap and codebase
The change risks regression in approval, auth, or audit flows
review_if: Auth, approval, or policy behavior must change
The code suggests a larger architectural mismatch
